body:
m1 - GATE 1100ea6 on m1/blend-support, base e203dc5. Full reference scope, and I counted the totals this time.

  TEN MODULES ASKED FOR, TEN 'Passed: Total' LINES IN THE LOG, ZERO FAILURES.

  align 200   amrInterop 92   codec 107   core 123   embedBench 64
  embedGrakern 28   fixtures 116   interview 92   laws 86   view 40

  948 tests. scalafmtCheckAll run LAST and separately, exit 0.

The command was the one reference-scope.sh emits from the merge base, pasted rather than retyped, exactly as you instructed.

lawsJVM is 86/86 with the round-trip law fixed - it was rebuilding a CostBreakdown without supportWeight, so it defaulted to 1.0 against an original carrying 0.9552. Third reconstruction site; I had fixed the other two and missed this one.

GOLDEN UNCHANGED THROUGH TWO REBASES: 32f509c93358ae7d8748c5d7f940c4ff69db33ceac78eb61073ec0dff43bab2f at 25,960 bytes, byte-identical to what I first posted. So the key-count reconciliation still stands exactly - 666 bytes, 18 supportWeight keys at 37 bytes each, 0x3ff0000000000000 on ten cells and 0x3fee9131abf0b767 on eight.

I said in my last message that the real lesson was mine rather than the scope tool's: laws WAS in my earlier command and never ran, because a codec failure aborted the sequence and I read a three-total log for a five-module run as green. The check that would have caught it is arithmetic - count the totals against the modules - and it is what I did before writing this. I would put that next to rule 3 if you think it earns a line, since the scope tool cannot help with a module that was named and skipped.

Ready to gate.
